summary.headline: Capri Global posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of INR353 crore (+102% YoY) on AUM of INR40,112 crore (+62% YoY) and cost-to-income of 44.2%.
summary.overview: Capri Global reported record quarterly profit after tax of INR353 crore, up 102% YoY, with consolidated AUM of INR40,112 crore, up 62% YoY and 10% QoQ. Gold loans (48% of AUM) drove growth, with AUM of INR19,179 crore (+111% YoY, +13% QoQ), while cost-to-income improved to 44.2% from 49.4% in Q4 FY26. Asset quality weakened at the margin: gross Stage 2 ratio rose to 3.8% from 2.8%, mostly on gold loans, and gross Stage 3 rose to 1.1%, largely from one construction finance account. Management revised its FY28 AUM target to INR65,000 crore and reiterated medium-term ROE of 19-21% and ROA of 4.2-4.7%.

financial_highlights.metric: Blended yield / spread on net advances

financial_highlights.change: Gross Stage 3 up INR74 crore QoQ

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR19,179 crore, +13% QoQ and +111% YoY; gross NPA 0.3%; 1,000 branches with productivity of INR19 crore per branch (from INR17 crore); disbursal LTV about 71%. Gold yield about 18.5%, management expects 50-75 bps more improvement.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: AUM INR6,779 crore, +24% YoY; disbursements INR616 crore, +32% YoY. Micro-LAP AUM INR876 crore. Share of AUM has declined as capital was prioritised to gold loans.

segments.name: Housing finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR7,815 crore, +42% YoY; self-employed customers about 75% of AUM; new South India branches disbursing about INR65 crore per month.

segments.name: Construction finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR6,332 crore, +40% YoY across 291 active projects; PCR raised to 70%; Stage 3 up INR31 crore QoQ on one account, with about INR30 crore recovered from an old NPA account.

segments.name: Co-lending and DA
segments.commentary: AUM INR8,126 crore, +74% YoY and +4% QoQ (20% of AUM); income INR65 crore, -8% YoY. 6 of 11 partner banks moved to CLM1 model.

segments.name: Car loan distribution and insurance
segments.commentary: Car loan origination INR3,282 crore, +43% YoY across 13 partner banks; insurance net fee income INR42 crore; 14 new insurance products launched via Capri Care.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM target of about INR50,000 crore; FY28 target raised to INR65,000 crore (30%+ CAGR), up from INR47,000 crore FY27 target previously cited by analysts.
Quarterly AUM additions of about INR3,000-3,500 crore, with the back half expected to be stronger.
Medium-term ROE 19-21% and ROA 4.2-4.7%, targeted by FY28 on a sustained basis.
Gold loan share of AUM to reach about 55% medium term; spreads expected to stabilise near 7.8%, possibly about 8% once gold loans exceed 50-53% of AUM.
Cost-to-income expected to hold at 44-45% over the next 12-18 months.
Cost of funds expected to remain broadly stable for the rest of FY27.
Branch rollout: 400 new gold loan branches to be operational by December 2026 (about 150 by Q2, the rest by Q3), revised up from 350.
capex_capacity: Gold loan branch network steady at 1,000 branches; 196 added in FY26 and 89 in Q4 FY26; total branch network 1,433 locations.
Plan to open about 400 branches in FY27, with 150-plus by end Q2 and the balance by Q3; longer-term plan of 400-500 openings a year.
16 MSME branches in Telangana and Karnataka to become operational from Q3 FY27.
Employee count up only 156 QoQ; AUM per employee INR3.4 crore vs INR1.8 crore a year earlier.
demand_pricing: Gold loan growth of about 25% is achievable from existing branches, with new branches adding further growth; a weak monsoon could raise gold loan demand from microfinance and marginal farmers.
Gold price fell about 4% QoQ; management says the 85% LTV trigger for auction notices and automated margin-call alerts limit risk.
Gold loan yields rose to about 18.5% from shift to smaller ticket sizes, with incentive plans changed accordingly.
Car loan origination growth moderated in the quarter; management is limiting volume to profitable unit economics, not cash-burn growth, with a used car loan pilot planned.
Co-lending volume growth slowed to 4% QoQ due to new co-lending guidelines and partner banks moving to CLM1.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the INR385 crore sequential Stage 2 rise by segment, whether it is recent origination or seasonal, why coverage fell from 11.8% to 9.4%, and any mix shift into gold.
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 2 rise: gold loans +INR373 crore, construction finance +INR13 crore, housing +INR15 crore, MSME +INR10 crore. Gold prices fell about 4% QoQ, driving more Stage 2 cases in gold. No direct answer on the coverage change in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR125 crore DCCO extension within the 0.7% construction finance GNPA, and is it real slippage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCCO cases are outside GNPA and still classified as standard.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of a weak or strong monsoon on gold loan demand.
qa_highlights.answer: A weak monsoon could push microfinance and marginal farmers to gold loans. Management said 25% gold loan growth is achievable from existing branches, with new branches adding further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Branch rollout: why Q1 additions were modest versus the earlier plan of about 350 branches in FY27, and whether additions are back-ended.
qa_highlights.answer: About 150 branches in Q2 and 250 more in Q3, for 400 total, now revised up from 350 and to be completed on or before December 2026. Management said the plan is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of gold loan yields at about 18.6%, and risk of competition.
qa_highlights.answer: Yields were about 18.5% after a shift to smaller tickets with changed incentives. Management expects another 50-75 bps of improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Scope for further cost-of-funds reduction in FY27.
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees little scope for further cost reduction from current levels in FY27, and expects costs to stay broadly stable. Diversification via NCDs, CP, bank refinancing and a GMTN programme is under way, with bank share to decline.

qa_highlights.question: Target gold loan share of AUM and FY27 and FY28 AUM targets, including quarterly run-rate.
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-term gold share of about 55% of AUM. FY27 target INR50,000 crore and FY28 INR65,000 crore, with quarterly additions of INR3,000-3,500 crore and the back half stronger. Product-wise disbursement split to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Leadership transitions and CEO vacancy.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said business heads are stable and attributed the movements to internal transfers of Head of Internal Audit, CCO and CFO to the housing subsidiary. It said there is no CEO vacancy and no plan to bring one in.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for achieving the 4.2-4.7% ROA and 19-21% ROE on a sustained basis.
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets these by FY28 on a consistent basis, even with 400-500 branch openings a year.

qa_highlights.question: Car loan origination moderation: profitability over growth, or demand or competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is limiting volume to profitable unit economics and not pursuing cash-burn growth. A used car loan pilot is planned, which should improve margins over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of 7.8% spreads and cost-to-income trajectory.
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads to stay around 7.8%, possibly about 8% once gold loans exceed 50-53% of AUM. Cost-to-income to remain at 44-45% for the next 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price correction risk, asset quality and risk controls.
qa_highlights.answer: Automated margin-call alerts trigger before auction notices at 85% LTV. Management sees no asset-quality risk from gold price falls, though further falls could slow growth.

qa_highlights.question: Average LTV on gold loans, and protection against gold price falls.
qa_highlights.answer: Average LTV at disbursement is about 71%, leaving a 29% cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the rise in construction finance GNPA and the outlook for asset quality.
qa_highlights.answer: One construction account slipped to NPA and was provided at about 70%. Management expects recovery within 6-9 months, with about INR30 crore recovered from an old NPA account in Q1. It says GNPA of 1.1% and net NPA of 0.6% will not fall further from here.

risks_watch: Gold prices: a 4% QoQ fall drove the INR373 crore gold Stage 2 increase, and gold price volatility could affect Stage 2 migration, LTV and growth.
Stage 2 ratio rose to 3.8% from 2.8%, and the consolidated provision coverage fell per the analyst's cited figures (11.8% to 9.4%); the company did not explain that drop on the call.
Construction finance: one account slipped to NPA; PCR raised to 70%. Watch whether recoveries (6-9 months) happen and whether further slippage follows.
Branch rollout: 400 branches due by December 2026 (150-plus by Q2); execution pace and the back-ended Q3 plan matter for the FY27 AUM target of INR50,000 crore.
Cost of funds guided stable in FY27; spread sustainability at 7.8% depends on gold mix rising toward 50-53%.
Co-lending volume growth slowed to 4% QoQ with partner banks moving to CLM1; car loan origination growth moderated in Q1.
Leadership churn and the absence of a CEO were raised; management said no CEO plan is in place.
key_quotes: I'm glad to share that Capri Global continued its track record of delivering strong performance quarter -on-quarter in Q1 FY27 with robust growth while achieving highest ever quarterly profit after tax of INR353 crores, a 102% increase year -on-year basis.
So, despite price fluctuation, we don't see any risk on the asset quality side.
There's no CEO position vacant. And there is no plan to bring any CEO.
So average gold to loan ratio at the disbursement level is about 71%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profitability and branch economics, citing record PAT and a 19-21% ROE target. Noticeably more cautious on asset quality (Stage 2 rise, construction NPA) and gold price risk, and less specific on the leadership and coverage questions.
